title: Fortune & Glory: The Cliffhanger Game
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=49KORRES2ks

Daniel (@dungeondive) has been away rehearsing with a new band for its first show. What he did play in the meantime was Fortune & Glory, Flying Frog's pulp cliffhanger game, which he sums up as "Indiana Jones the board game." He admits it is a table hog and tells Flying Frog, only half joking, to remember that they make games other than Shadows of Brimstone.

He plays it solo and co-op. Against the Mob is the easiest villain faction, and the Order of the Crimson Hand, a cult trying to resurrect old gods, is his thematic favourite. Heroes chase four relics around the world through a stack of challenge cards. The heart of the game is push-your-luck: after one success you can press on or make camp. If you press on and fail, the card flips to its Cliffhanger side, a harder test for a smaller reward, just like a serial that ends on a snapping rope.

He likes the sheer randomness (events, city encounters, dock tokens that can get you shanghaied) and even the shiny, cheap cards, which suit the pulp. The flowcharts look daunting, but a BGG cheat sheet makes it run smoothly. He closes on a new direction for the channel: buying less, going deeper on the games he loves, and maybe a long Warhammer Quest let's play.

----

Daniel loves how Fortune & Glory flips a failed test into a Cliffhanger rather than a plain loss. Which games have you seen turn failure into story instead of just a penalty?
